content.overview: A proposal (offer) when accepted becomes a promise. Communication, revocation, and acceptance rules under sections 3–9 determine when parties are bound.

sections.heading: Offer and invitation to treat
sections.body: An offer is capable of acceptance so as to form a promise. Catalogues, advertisements, and price lists are often invitations to treat, not offers.

sections.heading: Communication and revocation
sections.body: Communication of proposal, acceptance, and revocation follows sections 3–5. A proposal may be revoked before acceptance is complete as against the proposer. Acceptance must be absolute and unqualified (s. 7).

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Plead the communication chain: when the offer was made, how accepted, and whether revocation arrived in time. Electronic contracts need proof of dispatch and receipt under IT and BSA rules.
